source_text: Sunt quidem dulcia incitamenta vitiorum, amara etiam frequenter, quae a persecutoribus excitantur, tormenta poenarum, sed et illa censura honestatis everberat et ista consumit magnitudo patientiae.
pass_a_gloss: There are indeed sweet incitements of vices, bitter also frequently the torments of punishments which are excited by persecutors, but both those the censure of honesty beats back and these the greatness of patience consumes.
pass_b_english: Vices certainly have sweet enticements, and punishments inflicted by persecutors often bring bitter tortures. But the judgment of honor beats back the former, and the greatness of patience overcomes the latter.

choices.why: Julian's ethnic-rhetorical slur for Augustine; keep the geographic sting rather than neutralizing it.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
